in_hebrew.name: סלה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם סלה מקורו בשורש העברי סלע, שפירושו צור או אבן. הוא גם מתייחס למקום גבוה או לעיר מבוצרת. בספר תהילים, סלה הוא מונח המופיע פעמים רבות, בדרך כלל בסוף פסוקים, וייתכן שיהיה קשור להוראה מוזיקלית או לרגע של השתפכות רגשית. השם נושא משמעות של יציבות, חוזק וקדושה.

in_greek.name: Σела
in_greek.long_meaning: Τὸ ὄνομα Σела προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὴν ἑβραϊκὴ λέξη σלע, ἡ ὁποία σημαίνει πέτρα ἢ λίθος. Εἶναι ἐπίσης συνδεδεμένο μὲ τόπο ὑψηλὸ ἢ πόλη ἐνδυναμωμένη. Στὴν Καινή Διαθήκη, ὁ ὅρος Σела δὲν ἀναφέρεται ἐκτός ἀπὸ τὶς ψαλμῶν, ὅπου χρησιμοποιεῖται σὰν ὁδηγία μουσικὴ ἢ ροπή συναισθηματική. Τὸ ὄνομα μεταφέρει τὴ σημασία τῆς σταθερότητος, τῆς ἰσχύος καὶ τῆς ἁγιότητας.

in_latin.name: Sela
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Sela originem habet in voce hebrea סלע (sela), quae significat petram vel rupem. Etiam refertur ad locum elevatum aut urbem munitam. In Psalterio, Sela vox saepius occurrit, plerumque in fine versuum, fortasse musicae instructioni aut momenti emotionalis effusionis serviens. Nomen importat significationem firmitatis, fortitudinis et sanctitatis.

in_english.name: Sela
in_english.long_meaning: The name Sela originates from the Hebrew root סלע (sela), meaning rock or stone. It also refers to a high place or fortified city. In the Psalms, Sela appears frequently, often at the end of verses, likely serving as a musical instruction or a moment of emotional outpouring. The name carries connotations of stability, strength, and holiness. Historically, Sela has been used in various Christian traditions, symbolizing a solid foundation or a lofty spiritual aspiration. Today, it remains a meaningful choice for Christian parents seeking a name with deep biblical roots.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sela holds cultural significance in Hebrew, representing a strong and stable foundation or refuge. In the Middle East, rocks have long been considered a symbol of steadfastness and endurance, making this name a reflection of those attributes.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Sela also relates to its biblical origins. In the Old Testament, a woman named Sela is mentioned in the book of Genesis as the name given to a daughter of Abram and Hagar (Genesis 21:33). It is said that Sela lived in the desert near Beersheba, and this area became a well-known watering place in ancient Israel, providing sustenance and life.
